manifesto_l2.current: The sun does not choose who it reaches.
manifesto_l2.A: The sun spends itself on every room equally.
manifesto_l2.B: The sun cannot aim — it can only rise.
manifesto_l2.C: Every window in the city faces the same sun.

inscription.current: You warm every room you enter — and rarely ask who warms you.
inscription.A: You warm every room you enter — and run on warmth nobody returns.
inscription.B: You lift rooms before deciding to — and cannot switch it off to rest.
inscription.C: You are the weather of every room — and weather is never thanked.

dm_overview.A: Yang Fire gives off warmth the way a fire does, without checking who's nearby or what it costs to burn. Rooms pick up when you arrive. You make people feel more capable than they were an hour ago. What you don't do is refuel in public, and almost nobody thinks to ask.
dm_overview.B: Yang Fire works like a broadcast. The warmth transmits whether or not you meant to send it, and it reaches whoever happens to be in range. You commit to what lights you up and cool on what doesn't. Receiving is the skill that never got practiced, because giving always came first.
dm_overview.C: Yang Fire is the sun's kind of fire, the kind that rises whether anyone's watching. Every window in the building faces you. That's the gift and the whole problem. A sun doesn't get to pick its rooms, and nobody thanks the daylight.

yourNature_desc.current: You walk into a room and people feel more at ease, more energized, more capable — without you trying to make that happen. The cost is that you give it constantly and almost never get asked if you're okay.
yourNature_desc.A: You walk in and the room gets easier, braver, a little more possible. None of it is on purpose. The light just runs, all day, on you as fuel, and it says something that no one has ever thought to ask what it burns.
yourNature_desc.B: The room changes temperature before you've said a word, and that's not a decision, it's a property. You can't aim it and you can't switch it off. So you warm whoever's there, on whatever you've got left, even on the days there's nothing.
yourNature_desc.C: Rooms turn toward you the way fields turn toward morning. Nobody decides to, it's just what happens when the sun comes up. And like the sun, you only get looked at during an eclipse. Ordinary daylight never gets a thank-you.
